newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAA announces int'l cargo fuel surcharge.
newsitem.headline: SAA announces int'l cargo fuel surcharge.

text.p: South African Airways said on Monday it was introducing a fuel surcharge for air freight with effect from November 15.
The surcharge from South Africa will be 0.50 rand per kg while the surcharge from international points to South Africa will be $0.10 per kg or equivalent in local currency.
The state flag carrier said it had been forced to implement the surcharge due to rising costs.

"The price of jet fuel has increased drastically with world fuel market prices increasing by 50 percent during the period July-October 1996," Charles Fairweather, executive manager of SAA Cargo, said in a statement.

"The constant devaluation of the rand against the U.S. dollar is placing SAA Cargo under increasing financial pressure especially due to the fact that the fuel account represents a major expenditure for the airline."
The surcharge does not apply to SAA domestic services, minimum charges applicable to international shipments, published TACT rates and tariffs from South Africa to points in Africa.
